Name: Apache Log4j Remote Code Execution (Log4Shell)
Synopsis: The remote web application is vulnerable to remote code execution.
Description: Apache Log4j versions 2.0-beta9 through 2.14.1 JNDI features do not protect against attacker-controlled LDAP and other JNDI related endpoints. An attacker who can control log messages or log message parameters can execute arbitrary code loaded from LDAP servers.
Solution: Update Log4j to 2.17.1 or higher, or set log4j2.formatMsgNoLookups=true.
Plugin Output: JNDI lookup payload triggered DNS token callback on test-listener.

Name: OpenSSH Terrapin Attack Prefix Truncation Vulnerability
Synopsis: The SSH server uses cryptographic ciphers susceptible to sequence number manipulation.
Description: The Terrapin attack targets the SSH transport layer protocol to breach integrity sequence numbers during handshake negotiation.
Solution: Update OpenSSH to version 9.6p1 or newer, or disable ChaCha20-Poly1305 and CBC ciphers with ETM.
Plugin Output: Observed chacha20-poly1305@openssh.com cipher in SSH KEX negotiation.

Name: TLS 1.0 and 1.1 Deprecated Protocol Enabled
Synopsis: The remote service encrypts traffic using obsolete TLS protocols.
Description: The remote service accepts connections encrypted using TLS 1.0 or TLS 1.1. These protocol versions have known cipher suite deficiencies (BEAST, POODLE) and have been deprecated by RFC 8996.
Solution: Disable TLS 1.0 and TLS 1.1 in web server SSL configurations. Enforce TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3 exclusively.

Name: SNMP Agent Default Community Name (public)
Synopsis: The remote SNMP daemon responds to default community string 'public'.
Description: An unauthenticated attacker can query the SNMP agent using the default community name 'public' to enumerate interfaces, network topology, routing tables, and process lists.
Solution: Change or disable the default SNMP community strings in snmpd.conf.
